scope.topic: Explain how an enzyme and its substrate interact during catalysis.
scope.organism_context: General cell biology (no specific organism; generic cellular context)
included_processes: Substrate binding at the active site forming an enzyme-substrate complex
Induced fit between enzyme and substrate
Lowering of activation energy via the enzyme-substrate complex
excluded_processes: Environmental effects of temperature and pH on enzyme activity
Allosteric regulation by activators and inhibitors
Detailed kinetic models and rate equations
simplifications: The active site is treated as a single static region, though it undergoes a mild conformational shift (induced fit).
Multiple catalytic mechanisms (orientation, microenvironment, contortion, covalent participation) are grouped under 'lowering activation energy'.
The enzyme is depicted as returning to its original state after releasing product(s) without detailed intermediate steps.

support.quote: Almost all enzymes are proteins, comprised of amino acid chains, and they perform the critical task of lowering the activation energies of chemical reactions inside the cell.
The chemical reactants to which an enzyme binds are the enzyme’s substrates .
The location within the enzyme where the substrate binds is the enzyme’s active site .
When an enzyme binds its substrate, it forms an enzyme-substrate complex.
The enzyme-substrate complex can lower the activation energy by contorting substrate molecules in such a way as to facilitate bond-breaking, helping to reach the transition state.
After an enzyme catalyzes a reaction, it releases its product(s).
